annotations.annotation_text: Page 141 opens Book 1, Chapter 6 ("The Quiz Chapter") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones, featuring Shem, Shaun, Professor Jones, the Mookse, the Gripes. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 141 ("The Quiz Chapter"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "midden" on page 141 ("The Quiz Chapter"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. During this Age of Gods phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net
